indication.text: COBENFY is indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults.

citations.quote: COBENFY is indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults.

target_moa.text: Fixed combination of xanomeline, a muscarinic acetylcholine receptor agonist, and trospium chloride, a muscarinic antagonist. Xanomeline binds and activates muscarinic receptors (M1 to M5) with higher agonist activity at M1 and M4; efficacy in schizophrenia is thought to be due to M1/M4 agonism, while trospium antagonizes peripheral muscarinic receptors to improve tolerability.

citations.quote: KarXT is a combination of xanomeline, a muscarinic agonist, and trospium chloride, a muscarinic antagonist, indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults. Xanomeline binds to and activates muscarinic receptors in both the central and peripheral nervous systems.

Xanomeline is a direct muscarinic agonist that binds to muscarinic acetylcholine receptors M1 to M5 with comparable affinity (K_i) but exhibits higher agonistic activity (EC_{50}) at the M1 and M4 receptors.
Its efficacy is thought to be due to its agonist activity at M1 and M4 muscarinic acetylcholin
tissues, it is thought to help attenuate the muscarinic adverse reactions that are associated with xanomeline (see Section 9.1 for a review of the combination product and Study KAR-001).

modality.text: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination of two small molecules, xanomeline tartrate and trospium chloride)

citations.quote: Cobenfy is a fixed-combination product containing two small molecules, xanomeline tartrate and trospium chloride

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5% and at least twice placebo) were nausea (19% vs 4%), dyspepsia (18% vs 5%), constipation (17% vs 7%), vomiting (15% vs 1%), hypertension (11% vs 2%), abdominal pain, diarrhea, tachycardia, dizziness, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. COBENFY was associated with a mean increase in 24-hour heart rate of 9.8 bpm.
